STEP 2 - Ruler: The plate is a square-ish white dish, likely about 24 cm across. Its area is roughly 24 × 24 ≈ 550 cm² (rounded corners reduce this slightly, so about 500 cm²). In the image the plate spans about 345 px (x 220–565), so 1 cm ≈ 14 px.

STEP 3 - Items: One red-yellow apple (looks like a Pink Lady or Gala).

STEP 4 - Area: The apple is about 125 px wide, which is 125 / 14 ≈ 9 cm. Its footprint is 3.14 × 4.5² ≈ 63 cm², or about 12% of the plate. Food covers about 12% of the plate in total.

STEP 5 - Volume: A sphere of 8.5 cm diameter has volume 4/3 × 3.14 × 4.25³ ≈ 321 ml. An apple is slightly flattened and a 9 cm width may include some perspective enlargement, so I take about 8 cm diameter, which gives 268 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: Apple density is about 0.85 g/ml, so 268 × 0.85 ≈ 228 g. This fits a large apple of 200–230 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Apple with skin is about 52 kcal/100 g, so 228 g gives about 119 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: A large apple weighing about 220 g and giving about 115 kcal is plausible.
